significance.root_decision: For all n > 0 and 0 <= l <= n, the bipartite circulant graph G(n, l) has generic completion rank n - floor(sqrt(n(n - l))), the value predicted by the dimension count. This is Conjecture 5.6 of Bernstein, Blekherman and Sinn, who proved it for special families and named the step that was missing. The upper bound uses a new construction: Fourier vectors with an evenly spaced (Beatty) set of frequencies, so that each frequency class has at most d elements, and a Vandermonde system on the missing diagonals that forces the tangent map to be injective. The lower bound is the dimension count. Lean states generic completion rank literally, as a statement about a nonempty Zariski-open set of partial matrices in both directions, and proves the passage from a nonzero Jacobian minor to such an open set.
significance.caveat: Bounded literature search only. Cross-model confidence: correct 0.98, not public 0.85, not routine 0.75, Lean statement equals the printed conjecture 0.97. The printed formula omits a ceiling; the Lean formula n - Nat.sqrt(n(n - l)) equals the dimension-count prediction the conjecture names (checked for n <= 12). Closest later work: Dressler and Krone, arXiv:2010.09777, on real typical ranks of the same graphs, which does not prove the complex formula.
